## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pañcapaṇḍitajātaka* (Ja 508) is a canonical Jātaka tale whose full narrative is traditionally deferred in the commentary to the *Mahā-ummaggajātaka* (*Mahāummagge āvisabhavissati*) [Fausböll 1887]. The verses associated with the story address the theme of keeping a secret and the qualities of statecraft: the Bodhisatta advises the king never to disclose his secrets to anyone, contrasting with hostile counselors who argue that confiding in a wife, friend, brother, son, or mother is acceptable [Ānandajoti 2010]. Additional verse instruction emphasizes discerning profit and loss, recognizing what has been done and left undone, punishing those who deserve censure, and supporting those worthy of favor [Ānandajoti 2010].
